      "kind": "gotcha",
      "area": "tools",
      "summary": "An Actions run step with no shell key runs bash -e without pipefail: a failing left side of a pipe passes silently; name shell: bash for -eo pipefail.",

Applies to every piped run step, this repository's workflows and the seeded template's alike."

      "id": "houserules.actions-pinned-by-sha",
      "kind": "rule",
      "area": "tools",
      "summary": "Pin every workflow `uses:` to a full commit SHA, version tag as a comment; the Actions policy rejects a tag ref; release.yml pins live in dist-workspace.toml.",
      "body": [
        "The repository setting `sha_pinning_required` (Settings > Actions > General) fails any workflow run that references an action by tag or branch, and the allowed-actions policy is `selected`: GitHub-owned, verified creators, and the explicit patterns jdx/mise-action, googleapis/release-please-action, swatinem/rust-cache. A new action needs its pattern added there before its first run.",
        "Resolve a pin with the CLI, never from memory: `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<tag> --jq .sha`, then the precise tag for the comment from `repos/<owner>/<repo>/tags`. Dependabot (github-actions ecosystem) moves the SHA and the comment together on its weekly run.",
        "release.yml is generated (dist-workspace.toml is the source): add or bump a pin in `[dist.github-action-commits]` and run `dist generate`; `dist` picks the action version itself, so after a `cargo-dist-version` bump grep the regenerated file for any `uses:` without a 40-hex ref and pin it there."
      ],

        "release"

      "area": "tools",
      "summary": "A tag or commit pushed with the default GITHUB_TOKEN triggers no workflow; a release hand-off needs a PAT/App token or an explicit workflow_dispatch hop.",

Options recorded in the T5 doc: a PAT or GitHub App token on the tagging step, or a workflow_dispatch call gated on release_created output. The choice is an open phase-4 question for the owner."

      "id": "houserules.release-please-schema-gap",
      "kind": "gotcha",
      "area": "global",
      "summary": "release-please's config JSON schema omits prerelease-type and skip-snapshot from its root; keep those settings under the package entry.",
      "body": [
        "The schema at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/release-please/v17.11.2/schemas/config.json sets `additionalProperties: false` on the config root. The root's own `properties` list omits `prerelease-type` and `skip-snapshot`. `src/manifest.ts` reads both at the top level, like `versioning` and `release-type`. The project's docs show a top-level example with `prerelease-type`. The omission is a gap in the schema, not the runtime.",
        "Verified with `ajv-cli validate`. A root-level `prerelease-type` key fails with `params.additionalProperty: 'prerelease-type'` (`must NOT have additional properties`). The identical key nested under a `packages` entry validates cleanly: that path's value schema (`ReleaserConfigOptions`, reached through `allOf`) carries no such restriction.",
        "Put `prerelease-type`, `skip-snapshot`, and the other release settings under the package's own entry in `release-please-config.json` (`packages['crates/houserules']` as of HR-073, batch 20 T5; `packages['.']` before it), not at the config root. `src/manifest.ts` merges each package's config over the root default per key, so a single-package repository behaves identically either way. Only the nested placement passes the schema the file's own `$schema` points at."
      ],

        "schema",
        "config"

      "id": "process.wiring-checks-run-the-resolution",

      "kind": "rule",

    {
      "id": "quality.principles",
      "kind": "rule",
      "area": "global",
      "standing": true,
      "summary": "YAGNI, KISS, DRY; prefer a well-maintained library to custom code; one responsibility per unit; tests assert behavior; a11y and i18n are part of done.",
      "body": [
        "YAGNI: build only what the current backlog item needs.",
        "KISS: choose the simplest design that meets the requirement. No abstraction for one caller, no option without a second use, no layer that only forwards.",
        "DRY once logic has two real call sites: never leave a copy that can drift (shared constants, option factories, one write path). One call site is not yet duplication.",
        "Prefer a well-maintained library (vetted, exact-pinned) to a custom implementation of a solved problem: parsing, validation, globbing, dates, retries. A standing project decision may rule an exception; record it as an entry.",
        "One responsibility per file and per function. Each unit boundary is one a reader can understand without its internals.",
        "Tests assert behavior, not implementation details, and can fail. Clean up global and module state (mocks, prototypes) after each test.",
        "A dedicated compliance pass over the existing codebase is its own backlog item; new code complies immediately.",
        "Tests assert behavior, not implementation details, and can fail. Clean up global and module state (mocks, prototypes) after each test; an auto-restore setting covers only spies, so a mock created in a module-mock factory gets its own explicit afterEach reset.",
        "Re-implementing another engine's input language (regex syntax, glob syntax) is the canonical build-vs-library violation: validity verdicts come from an engine of that language; a hand-rolled scan may only choose message wording after the engine has decided (batch 16: the glob translator missed nested braces and panicked; the regex scan flipped four verdicts against V8)."
      ],

        "quality"

    {
      "id": "security-hygiene.exact-pins",
      "kind": "rule",
      "area": "global",
      "standing": true,
      "summary": "Pin exact versions. Install only with a CLI (`cargo add <crate>@=<version>`, `pnpm add --save-exact`). Never write a version number by hand.",
      "body": [
        "Ranges (`^`, `~`) widen the attack surface. Resolve to the latest stable version at install time.",
        "The deterministic check covers `package.json` and `Cargo.toml`; ranges inside the `engines` object are floors, not dependency pins, and are exempt. Other ecosystems are judged by the reviewer under the same rule.",
        "A bare Cargo range (\"2.14\", an implicit caret) is invisible to the pattern without false-positiving the [package] version line; it stays judged material (batch 17: a Cargo dependency landed while the check read zero files)."
      ],
      "tags": [
        "dependencies",
        "supply-chain"

        "date": "2026-08-30",

        "type": "grep-absent",
        "level": "fail",
        "files": [

          "**/Cargo.toml"

        "pattern": "(?<!\"engines\":\\s*\\{[^}]*)(\"([\\^~]|>=?|<=?)\\s*\\d|\"\\*\"|\"latest\"|\"\\d+(\\.\\d+)*\\.x\")",
        "scope": "changed"

    {
      "id": "writing-style.doc-comments",
      "kind": "rule",
      "area": "global",
      "standing": true,
      "summary": "Document every exported symbol with the language's doc-comment convention. Name things so the code reads without comments.",
      "body": [
        "A doc comment states what the item is for, its invariants, and what it returns or raises when the signature does not say so. It never restates the signature.",
        "Conventions: TSDoc in TypeScript, JSDoc in JavaScript, rustdoc in Rust, docstrings in Python — the language's standard form.",
        "Self-documenting code first: full words, verbs for functions, `is`/`has` for booleans, no abbreviation a newcomer must decode, one meaning per name. A comment that explains a name means the name is wrong.",
        "Comments inside a body still follow writing-style.code-comments: only for a constraint the code cannot show.",
        "A doc comment stating a behavior ('returns tracked files', 'exits 0 on clean') is a claim under process.claims-match-artifacts - re-read it against the symbol at HEAD in the same pass that edits the symbol (batch 21 T1: a function documented as the tracked-file list walked the whole disk)."
      ],
      "tags": [
        "docs",
        "comments",
        "naming"
      ],

    {
      "id": "writing-style.principles",
      "kind": "rule",
      "area": "global",
      "standing": true,
      "summary": "Write docs, comments, commit messages, and reports in ASD-STE100 style: short sentences, active voice, one instruction per sentence, concise.",
      "body": [
        "Sources: Williams, *Style*; Gopen & Swan, \"The Science of Scientific Writing\". They apply on top of ASD-STE100.",
        "Make the main character the subject and its action the verb.",
        "Unpack nominalizations into verbs: \"perform validation of\" becomes \"validate\".",
        "Delete expletives (\"there is\", \"it is\"), filler (\"in order to\", \"the fact that\", \"note that\"), and hedges that carry no information.",
        "Put old information in the topic position, new information in the stress position.",
        "Keep subject and verb adjacent.",
        "End on the emphasis."
      ],
      "tags": [
        "docs",
        "style"
      ],
